To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have determined the complete nucleotide sequence for the gene encoding E. coli tryptophan-tRNA synthetrase and that we have used the deduced amino acid sequences to map the locations of mutations in the enzyme.

the nucleotide sequence of E. coli tryptophan-tRNA synthetese is 60% identical to the sequence of the Bacillus enzyme; that we have predicted the secondary structure of both enzymes and have compared these structures to the known three-dimensional structures of other synthetases; and that we have mapped several missense mutations within the E. coli gene to regions of the enzyme that are important for its catalytic function.
we sequenced the gene for tryptophanyl-transfer RNA synthetase from E. coli, and that we determined the location of missense mutations in the gene.

the structure, function and evolution of aminoacyl-tRNAsynthetases and the tRNAs that they aminoacylate.
the molecular biology and enzymology of tryptophanyl tRNA synthetase and its cognate tRNA.
understanding the molecular mechanisms of protein synthesis and with understanding how mutations affect the function of a specific enzyme.

we have determined the complete nucleotide sequence for the trpS gene of E. coli, have used this sequence to predict the primary and secondary structure of the enzyme, have mapped a series of mutations that affect the enzyme in different ways, and have used this information to identify regions of the enzyme that are likely to be functionally important.
